newsitem.title: FRENCH POLYNESIA: Polynesia pays tribute to Kon Tiki.
newsitem.headline: Polynesia pays tribute to Kon Tiki.

text.p: French Polynesia on Thursday celebrated the 50th anniversary of the voyage of Kon Tiki, a raft built to traditional Inca designs that sailed from Peru, across the South Pacific, to its shores.

Norwegian ethnologist Thor Heyerdahl, now 82, and six crew members set off from the Peruvian port of Callao on April 27, 1947, in a balsa wood raft, in an attempt to show that the ancestors of the South Pacific islanders could have sailed from South America.
On August 7, 1947, 101 days and 4,300 miles (6,880 km) later they arrived safely at the coral reef of Rarola atoll, in Polynesia's Tuamotu archipelago.
Heyerdahl's theory was subsequently proven wrong, but the adventure caught the imagination of people around the world in the early post-war years and has remained a legend since.
French Polynesia's postal service issued a commemorative stamp and telephone card bearing a picture of the raft to mark Thursday's anniversary.
